text.p: The following are the main stories from Friday morning's Austrian newspapers.
- The gap between high and low income earners has widened, a study by economic research institute IHS says. Austria needs more qualified personnel for which an educational offensive is necessary.
- All shops will be able to be open 66 hours a week, as opposed to the current limit of 60 hours for the majority, according to a draft version of controversial new legislation on shop hours.
- Austria's biggest baker Anker expects profits to halve to 20 million schillings in 1996.
- Carton maker Mayr-Melnhof has signed a joint-venture with Singaporean Pulp and Paper Company
- Creditanstalt expects profits to be 20 percent higher in 1996. In the first three quarters net profit rose 9.8 percent to 4.648 billion schillings.
- IHS chief Bernahrd Felderer says changes must be made in Austria's pension system, or it will collapse by 2030.
- Brickmaker Wienerberger reported a 20 percent drop in nine-month profit on Thursday to 1.041 billion. The company plans an ADR listing in the United States in the near future. KURIER
- Steel maker Vogel & Noot Holding AG will sell off two of its loss-making units to employees through a management-buyout.
- Finance Minister Viktor Klima has said that no new spending cuts will be made in 1997.
- Austria is always the last of the 15 European Union members to introduce new EU-legislation.
